title: A bounded rejecting computation
statement: Let $e$ be either Boolean value, and let $z,w,t$ be Boolean words with $z=\mathrm{dbl}(w)\mathbin{++}t$. Suppose either $t$ is empty, $t$ consists of a single bit, or $t$ begins with the two-bit block $10$. Then the circuit-evaluation machine with exactness flag $e$, started on input $z$, reaches within $2|w|+2$ steps a halted configuration whose output is the one-bit word $0$.
hypotheses_covered: The tail $t$ is empty, has length one, or begins with $10$
